B1L08-G01-P185.title: Use 好 or 難 with perception verbs or action verbs to complete the following sentences.

repairs.note: You like the movie a lot, so it is good to watch: 好看.
A movie is watched: 看.
The verb follows 好: 好看.
好 comes first, right before the verb: 好看.

items.fallbackRepair: 好/難 + verb: 好看.

result.traditional: 這部電影很好看，我很喜歡。
result.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng hěn hǎokàn, wǒ hěn xǐhuān.
result.english: This movie is very good; I like it a lot.
result.simplified: 这部电影很好看，我很喜欢。

items.prompt: You really like this movie. What is it like?

repairs.note: You can ride it for a long time without getting tired: 好騎.
The question is how it rides: 騎.

result.pinyin: Xīn de jiǎotàchē hěn hǎoqí.

repairs.note: Friends learned it in one lesson, so it is easy to learn: 好學.
You want to learn it too, so the verb is 學.
The verb follows 好: 好學.

repairs.note: He drew it badly, so it doesn’t look good: 難看.
A picture is looked at: 看.
The verb follows 難: 難看.
難 comes first, right before the verb: 難看.

items.fallbackRepair: 好/難 + verb: 難看.

result.traditional: 我覺得這張畫他畫得不好，有點兒難看。

repairs.note: Everyone wants a cup, so it tastes good: 好喝.

repairs.note: Three maps and you still can’t find it: 難找.

segments.traditional: 他為什麼常常穿綠色的衣服？
segments.simplified: 他为什么常常穿绿色的衣服？

repairs.note: 為什麼 asks why. You are giving the reason and the result: 因為…所以….
The reason comes first, with 因為; 所以 starts the result.
The result comes second, with 所以; 因為 starts the reason.

items.fallbackRepair: Reason first with 因為, result second with 所以.

result.traditional: 因為他喜歡綠色，所以他常常穿綠色的衣服。
result.simplified: 因为他喜欢绿色，所以他常常穿绿色的衣服。
result.pinyin: Yīnwèi tā xǐhuān lǜsè, suǒyǐ tā chángcháng chuān lǜsè de yīfu.
result.english: Because he likes green, he often wears green clothes.

items.prompt: Why does he often wear green? (He likes green.) Build your answer: reason, then result.

segments.traditional: 因為我想游泳，也想曬太陽，所以想去海邊玩。
segments.simplified: 因为我想游泳，也想晒太阳，所以想去海边玩。

repairs.note: 所以 introduces a result. To ask for a reason, use 為什麼.
因為 gives a reason; you are asking for one: 為什麼.

items.fallbackRepair: To ask for a reason, use 為什麼.

result.pinyin: Nǐ wèishénme xiǎng qù hǎibiān wán?

items.prompt: Ask your friend why they want to go to the beach.

B1L08-G05-P195.title: Complete the sentences with 快（要）/要……了.

scene.alt: Two calendars: today is April 3; the other date is April 5.

repairs.note: Today is April 3 and the visit is April 5, not tomorrow: something close ahead is 快要…了.
He isn’t here now; he comes in two days: 快要…了.
快要 comes first, before what is about to happen; 了 closes it: 我的日本朋友快要來了。
了 closes the sentence; 快要 comes before the action: 我的日本朋友快要來了。

items.fallbackRepair: About to happen: 快要 before the action, 了 at the end.

result.traditional: 我的日本朋友快要來了。
result.pinyin: Wǒ de Rìběn péngyǒu kuàiyào lái le.
result.english: My Japanese friend is coming soon.
result.simplified: 我的日本朋友快要来了。

items.prompt: Today is April 3. Your Japanese friend comes on April 5. Build the sentence.

scene.alt: Two clocks: now is 11:50; the noon break starts at 12:00.

repairs.note: It’s 11:50 and the break starts at 12:00, so it hasn’t started yet: 快要…了.
The break is ten minutes away, today, not tomorrow: 快要…了.
快要 comes first, before what is about to happen; 了 closes it: 我們快要休息了。
了 closes the sentence; 快要 comes before the action: 我們快要休息了。

items.fallbackRepair: About to happen: 快要 before the action, 了 at the end.

result.pinyin: Wǒmen kuàiyào xiūxí le.
result.english: We are about to take a break.

items.prompt: It’s 11:50. The break starts at 12:00. Build the sentence.

scene.alt: Two calendars: today is October 1; younger brother’s tenth birthday is October 10.

repairs.note: He turns ten on October 10, not now: 快要…了.
Today is October 1; his birthday is October 10: 快要…了.
快要 comes first, before what is about to happen; 了 closes it: 弟弟快要十歲了。
了 closes the sentence; 快要 comes before the action: 弟弟快要十歲了。

items.fallbackRepair: About to happen: 快要 before the action, 了 at the end.

result.pinyin: Dìdi kuàiyào shí suì le.
result.english: My younger brother is about to turn ten.

items.prompt: Today is October 1. Your brother turns ten on October 10. Build the sentence.
